summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable (decision: not_2d_applicable, simulation_allowed false, comparison_valid false). Studio did not run; simulation status is 'skipped' because the custom experiment has no floorplan blocks and no power_w object, so there is no Studio result and no transient trace. The scenario is the paper's steady-state HotSpot comparison of a 1 MiB MemPool 2D SoC against a 3D face-to-face memory-on-logic stack, with reported Tmax above a 27 C ambient of 46 C (2D), 55 C (3D memory die) and 57 C (3D logic die). Because nothing ran, no Studio temperature can be compared with the 57 C logic-die observable or the other paper values, and no agreement or disagreement can be claimed. Essential physical mismatches would also block a numerical comparison even if a run were forced: a two-tier stacked geometry cannot be represented by a planar 2D die, the full package and two-sided heat path (TIM, spreader, heatsink at 0.17 K/W, substrate, PCB at 50 K/W) is not reproduced, size-dependent silicon conductivity (100 W/m-K for the 5 um logic die) is not captured, and no block-level floorplan or per-block power is published. The extracted evidence is only a record of the paper's stated parameters; it does not constitute a replication. Qualitatively, the paper reports that the 3D stack runs hotter than 2D, driven by roughly 1.37x higher power density, but this is the paper's claim and has not been tested here. The input and scientific gates failed, evidence locators and linked assets are unpinned, and adversarial and independent reviews are unresolved, so the final verdict stays at no valid comparison and no exact replication is claimed.
limitations: Studio did not run (skipped: custom experiment has no blocks and no power_w), so there is no simulated result and no transient trace; the custom 2D steady experiment is empty.
The gate verdict is not_2d_applicable with comparison_valid false; no numerical comparison to the 46, 55 or 57 C paper values is made.
The 3D F2F memory-on-logic stack with two tiers, a 2.85 um BEOL layer and a 5 um thinned logic die cannot be represented by a planar 2D die.

The package stack (7 W/m-K TIM, spreader, heatsink at 0.17 K/W, C4 bumps, substrate, solder balls, underfill, PCB at 50 K/W) and the HotSpot boundary conditions are not matched to any Studio cooling model.
Size-dependent silicon conductivity (140 and 100 W/m-K) is not reproduced by a bulk-silicon model.

No block-level floorplan coordinates or per-block powers are published; only the 40 W 2D TDP, the 0.913x 3D scaling and an unreadable pie chart are given, so inputs cannot be built without inventing data.
Evidence entries lack valid page or pinned asset locators; the HotSpot repository link is a URL only and not a pinned asset, and no MemPool configuration or power files exist in the packet.
Adversarial methods, code, parameters, config and data checks and the independent page/asset review are unresolved, so extracted values are unverified.
The Tmax values were read from figure labels and text rather than tables, and some ambiguities remain (mm2 vs mm unit notation, 0.665 vs 0.667 footprint scale, inferred 1 MiB capacity for Fig. 4).
Temperatures are rises above a 27 C ambient and the HotSpot solver and meshing differ from Studio's; exact replication is not claimed.
A custom experiment needs 1–128 blocks and a power_w object
